from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
x = {(p,w): m.addVar(lb=0, vtype='C') for p in ['P1','P2'] for w in ['D1','D2','D3']}
# Supply: P1=1000, P2=1500
# Demand: D1=80, D2=90, D3=80 (assuming no box conversion for this test of the constraint logic)
for p in ['P1','P2']:
    m.addCons(quicksum(x[p,w] for w in ['D1','D2','D3']) <= {'P1':1000,'P2':1500}[p])
for w in ['D1','D2','D3']:
    m.addCons(quicksum(x[p,w] for p in ['P1','P2']) == {'D1':80,'D2':90,'D3':80}[w])
# The suspicious constraint: x[P2,w] <= 20 for each w
for w in ['D1','D2','D3']:
    m.addCons(x['P2',w] <= 20)
m.setObjective(quicksum(x[p,w] for p in ['P1','P2'] for w in ['D1','D2','D3']), 'minimize')
m.optimize()
print('Status with per-warehouse cap 20:', m.getStatus())
"
